svg.text: Jane has been a bridesmaid 27 times
she shares a cab with a man in a tux
▸ MEET-CUTE — an entrance, not a marriage
George is back from the climbing trip
Kevin writes the column Jane despises
Six months in Europe, one engagement party
Tess catches George before Jane can speak
Vegetarian, dogs, the outdoors — all borrowed
their mother's dress goes to Tess
▸ BFF — Casey, doing the actual work
Jane plans her own dream wedding for her sister
Malcolm Doyle turns out to be Kevin
▸ the scene the film is remembered for
The piece runs without her knowing
she ends it, and she is not wrong to
▸ BREAKUP — it flows from who he is
Tess cuts up the dress; Jane retaliates
George sees the dishonesty and cancels
she quits, and the crush has gone quiet
She finds him at somebody else's wedding
and says it first, in front of strangers
▸ GESTURE — and it is hers, not his
wearing what Jane wore at their weddings
LANES — label size follows strand width
“the dresses” is the title object, not a person. Hatched lane = off-page.
Six lanes, eleven beats, 111 minutes. Time runs down the page.
Row spacing widens before the coda — a year passes there.
Each beat is tagged with the rubric category it earns, so this doubles as the anchor's scoring sheet.
The house: 27 of 30, a nominal 100%. You don't ding the house the party's at.
Ebert's three: left unpicked. Whether the house is a true 27 is still under review.
